# Minecraft Server Hosting — Product Options Research (Aug 2026)

**Critical current-state note:** Mojang switched to **year-based versioning in 2026**. The 1.21.x line was followed by **26.1 (Tiny Takeover, March 2026)**, then **26.2 (Chaos Cubed, June 2026)** — the current stable release. **26.3** is in snapshot testing (since June 23, 2026), targeting Q3 2026. Modern versions run on **Java 25**. Any version picker hardcoded to "1.x" is now stale.
Sources: [minecraft.wiki version history](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_version_history), [minecraft.net numbering change](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-new-version-numbering-system)

---

## 1. Editions / Versions to offer as a picker

**Edition (top-level fork):** Java vs Bedrock. These are different acquisition + runtime paths entirely — Bedrock is NOT plugin/mod compatible with Java software.

**Java server software / modloaders to offer as choices:**

| Software | Type | 2026 status / when to recommend |
|---|---|---|
| **Vanilla** | Base | Reference/purist. Mojang jar. |
| **Paper** | Plugin server (Spigot fork) | **The default recommendation.** Most-used; best perf + plugin API. Now served via Fill v3 API. |
| **Purpur** | Paper fork | Paper + hundreds of extra gameplay/config toggles. Runs all Paper plugins (`paper-api`). |
| **Pufferfish** | Paper fork | Extra performance patches, some experimental. |
| **Leaf** | Pufferfish fork (new, late-2024→2025) | Aggressive optimizations + Folia back-ports. Worth offering as an "advanced/experimental" pick. |
| **Folia** | Paper regionized-threading fork | Multi-core ticking for **very large** player counts. **Not a drop-in** — most plugins need explicit Folia support. Niche/advanced only. |
| **Spigot / Bukkit / CraftBukkit** | Legacy plugin servers | Offer for legacy compatibility; Paper supersedes both. Spigot must be self-compiled via BuildTools (licensing) — most hosts ship it but Paper is preferred. |
| **Fabric** | Lightweight modloader | Modern modding, best for performance mods + newer versions. |
| **Forge** | Modloader | For **older** packs (1.12.2, 1.16.5, 1.19.2, many 1.20.1). |
| **NeoForge** | Forge fork | **The de-facto standard for 1.20.2+ / 1.21+ / 26.x modding.** ~93% of popular mods target it; most new mods are NeoForge-first. APIs diverged from Forge at 1.20.2 — mods are NOT cross-compatible. |
| **Quilt** | Fabric fork | Minority alternative modloader; offer but low demand. |

**Modpack platforms (one-click):** CurseForge modpacks (`.zip`), Modrinth modpacks (`.mrpack`), Feed The Beast (FTB), ATLauncher. See §2 for install mechanics.

**How version selection should work:**
- **Java:** Populate release versions dynamically from the software's own API (never hardcode). Offer: *latest stable* (default), a *specific release version* dropdown, and an optional *snapshots / pre-releases / experimental channel* toggle (Paper Fill v3 exposes `alpha`/`beta`/`stable`/`recommended` channels).
- **Bedrock:** Version-pin explicitly. Bedrock clients auto-update and refuse to connect to mismatched servers, so the server version must track the current client — pin to a known-good build and surface an "update available" prompt rather than silent auto-update (which can break worlds/addons).

**Recommendation defaults to bake in:** Paper = default Java pick; NeoForge = default for modded 1.21+/26.x; Forge only when the target version is old; Fabric for perf-focused/lightweight modded.
Sources: [ModReady NeoForge standard](https://modready.gg/news/neoforge-new-standard-modded-minecraft), [Campfire NeoForge vs Forge](https://campfirehosting.com/guides/neoforge-vs-forge), [CodeRoasis server software guide 2026](https://coderoasis.com/minecraft-server-software-complete-guide-2026/), [Paper Fill v3 downloads](https://docs.papermc.io/misc/downloads-service/)

---

## 2. Top mods/plugins ecosystem (one-click expectations)

**Plugin/mod platforms to integrate for one-click browse+install:**
- **Modrinth** (open API, `.mrpack` modpacks, plugins + mods) — best API for automation.
- **CurseForge** (largest catalog; requires API key for programmatic download).
- **Hangar** (PaperMC's official plugin platform).
- **SpigotMC / Bukkit resources** (legacy but still huge for plugins).

**Bukkit/Spigot/Paper plugins owners expect one-click (the "starter set"):**
- **EssentialsX** — 100+ commands: homes, warps, kits, teleport, economy hooks. Near-universal.
- **LuckPerms** — industry-standard permissions (Spigot/Paper/Velocity).
- **WorldEdit** — in-game world editing.
- **WorldGuard** — region protection (pairs with WorldEdit).
- **GriefPrevention** — claim-based grief protection (alternative to WorldGuard for survival).
- **Vault** — economy/permissions bridge API (dependency for many plugins).
- **PlaceholderAPI** — placeholder bridge (dependency for many plugins).
- **CoreProtect** — block logging / rollback / anti-grief.
- **Dynmap** and/or **BlueMap** — live web maps (BlueMap = modern 3D, Dynmap = classic 2D).
- **spark** — performance profiler (owners + support use it constantly).
- **Geyser + Floodgate** — **cross-play: let Bedrock clients join a Java server** (Geyser = protocol bridge, Floodgate = auth without a Java account). One of the highest-impact additions for a public server.
- **ViaVersion + ViaBackwards (+ ViaRewind)** — let clients on newer (or older) versions connect to a differently-versioned server.
- **DiscordSRV** — Discord ↔ in-game chat bridge.
- **ProtocolLib** — protocol library dependency for many plugins.

**Fabric/Forge/NeoForge performance mods (server-side) owners expect:**
- **Lithium** — general game-logic optimization (the flagship).
- **FerriteCore** — memory reduction 40–50%, big for large modpacks.
- **Krypton** — networking-stack optimization (~up to 40% less networking CPU).
- **C2ME** — parallel/multi-core chunk generation + loading.
- **ModernFix** — all-in-one perf + memory + bug fixes, works across loaders.
- **Starlight** — light-engine rewrite (only needed <1.20; merged into vanilla since 1.20 / superseded by ScalableLux on newer).
- (Client-side FPS mods like Sodium/Iris/Entity Culling are player-side, not server — but a host wiki should mention them.)

**Modpack one-click installs** — build all four flows:
- **Modrinth** `.mrpack`: use `mrpack-install` (open-source CLI, `nothub/mrpack-install`) or the Modrinth API. Cleanest to automate.
- **CurseForge** `.zip`: resolve mods via CurseForge API (needs API key); installer auto-installs the correct Forge/Fabric/NeoForge loader, then downloads mods + configs.
- **FTB** and **ATLauncher**: expose their server-pack downloads; both distribute server-side install scripts.

The one-click UX (per Nodecraft/WiseHosting model): user pastes/selects a pack → panel installs the correct loader version → downloads mods + config → sets memory. Offer a searchable in-panel modpack browser backed by Modrinth + CurseForge search APIs.
Sources: [ApexMinecraftHosting best plugins 2026](https://apexminecrafthosting.com/guides/minecraft/plugins/recommended-plugins/), [Teramont best plugins 2026](https://teramont.net/blog/best-minecraft-server-plugins-2026), [WiseHosting optimization mods](https://wisehosting.com/blog/10-best-minecraft-server-optimization-mods), [mrpack-install](https://github.com/nothub/mrpack-install), [Nodecraft modpack import](https://nodecraft.com/support/games/minecraft/mods/how-to-import-your-own-modpack-from-curseforge-and-modrinth), [Modrinth modpacks](https://support.modrinth.com/en/articles/8802250-modpacks-on-modrinth)

---

## 3. Key editable config files + high-value keys

**`server.properties`** (all Java software) — expose these 12–15 as first-class wizard fields:
1. `max-players`
2. `difficulty` (peaceful/easy/normal/hard)
3. `gamemode` (survival/creative/adventure/spectator)
4. `hardcore` (true/false)
5. `level-seed`
6. `level-type` (`minecraft:normal` / `flat` / `large_biomes` / `amplified`)
7. `motd` (server list description)
8. `pvp` (true/false)
9. `view-distance` (chunks — biggest perf lever)
10. `simulation-distance` (chunks — mob/tick radius, biggest perf lever)
11. `spawn-protection`
12. `online-mode` (true = require Mojang auth; **false only behind a proxy/BungeeCord** — never expose cracked to internet)
13. `allow-flight` (true prevents anti-cheat kicks with fly plugins/elytra)
14. `white-list` / `enforce-whitelist`
15. `max-world-size`, `allow-nether`, `enable-command-block`, `resource-pack` + `require-resource-pack`, `server-port`, `query.port`/`enable-query`, `enable-rcon`+`rcon.password` (needed for remote console).

**`eula.txt`** — `eula=true` (must auto-accept on first provision or server won't start; surface the Mojang EULA in the wizard).

**Access-control JSON files** (edit via panel UI, not raw): `ops.json` (operators), `whitelist.json`, `banned-players.json`, `banned-ips.json`.

**Paper (1.20+) — two files:** `config/paper-global.yml` and `config/paper-world-defaults.yml` (per-world override: `paper-world.yml`). High-value keys:
- `per-player-mob-spawns: true` (fairer, prevents farm hijacking spawn budget)
- despawn ranges (`entities.spawning.despawn-ranges` — soft/hard, e.g. soft 28 / hard 96)
- entity/tile-entity tick tuning, `max-auto-save-chunks-per-tick`
- redstone implementation (`ALTERNATE_CURRENT`)
- view/no-tick view distance overrides, anti-xray, `use-faster-eigencraft-redstone`.

**`spigot.yml`** (applies under Paper too): `mob-spawn-range`, `entity-activation-range` (animals/monsters/misc), `merge-radius` (items/exp), `ticks-per` (animal/monster/water spawns, autosave), `view-distance`, entity-tracking ranges.

**`bukkit.yml`**: `spawn-limits` (monsters/animals/water-animals/ambient), `ticks-per` autosave/spawn, `chunk-gc`.

**Purpur:** adds `purpur.yml` with hundreds of extra gameplay toggles.

**Fabric / Forge / NeoForge:** per-mod configs live in `config/` (e.g. `config/<modid>.toml`/`.json`/`.json5`), plus loader files (`user_jvm_args.txt` for NeoForge). Expose a file-manager + text editor for these rather than field-mapping every mod.

**Bedrock:** its own `server.properties` (different keys), plus `permissions.json`, `allowlist.json` (whitelist), and `.mcaddon`/behavior+resource pack folders.
Sources: [PaperMC configuration reference](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/reference/configuration/), [Paper world config](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/reference/world-configuration/), [spigot.yml reference](https://docs.papermc.io/paper/reference/spigot-configuration/), [Wabbanode best Paper settings 2026](https://wabbanode.com/blog/minecraft/best-paper-settings-for-performance)

---

## 4. Server acquisition mechanism (Minecraft is NOT on SteamCMD)

There is **no SteamCMD app ID** — Minecraft servers are never distributed through Steam. Each software has its own acquisition path:

**Vanilla Java (Mojang):**
- Manifest: `https://piston-meta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest_v2.json` (mirror: `https://launchermeta.mojang.com/mc/game/version_manifest_v2.json`)
- That lists every version → each entry's `url` points to a per-version JSON at `https://piston-meta.mojang.com/v1/packages/<hash>/<version>.json`
- That version JSON's `downloads.server.url` gives the server jar at `https://piston-data.mojang.com/v1/objects/<hash>/server.jar` (SHA1-verifiable).
- Start: `java -Xmx<N>G -Xms<N>G -jar server.jar nogui`

**Paper (and same shape for Velocity/Waterfall/Folia):** **Fill v3 API** — `api.papermc.io/v2` was frozen Dec 31, 2025.
- Versions: `GET https://fill.papermc.io/v3/projects/paper`
- Builds: `GET https://fill.papermc.io/v3/projects/paper/versions/{VERSION}/builds`
- Download URL is embedded in the build's response (`downloads` → `url`, on `fill-data.papermc.io`); filter `channel == "STABLE"`. **Requires a descriptive `User-Agent` header.** GraphQL also available at `https://fill.papermc.io/graphql`.
- Purpur has its own API (`api.purpurmc.org/v2/purpur`); Pufferfish/Leaf via their Jenkins/CI or GitHub releases.

**Fabric:** meta API at `https://meta.fabricmc.net`
- Game versions: `/v2/versions/game`; loader: `/v2/versions/loader`; installer: `/v2/versions/installer`
- Direct server-launcher jar: `https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/loader/{GAME}/{LOADER}/{INSTALLER}/server/jar` — this launcher self-downloads Fabric + the vanilla server on first run.

**Forge:** installer jars from Forge Maven / files.minecraftforge.net; run `java -jar forge-<ver>-installer.jar --installServer`. Newer versions produce a `run.sh`/`run.bat` + `user_jvm_args.txt`.

**NeoForge:** installer from Maven — `https://maven.neoforged.net/releases/net/neoforged/neoforge/{VERSION}/neoforge-{VERSION}-installer.jar`; run `java -jar neoforge-<ver>-installer.jar --installServer` (auto-detects headless). Produces `run.sh` + `user_jvm_args.txt`. Also `neoforged/ServerStarterJar` for direct-start jars.

**Bedrock Dedicated Server (BDS):** ZIP from `https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/download/server/bedrock` (Windows + Linux/Ubuntu 22.04+ builds). No Java. Extract ZIP → edit `server.properties` → run `./bedrock_server` (Linux binary; needs `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.`). Version history mirrors: mcbds.reh.tw. Note the download page is gated behind a EULA/robots check — scrape carefully or use a version-index mirror.

**Aikar's flags (GC tuning, Java servers):** The community-standard G1GC flag set Paper documents as baseline — reduces TPS/GC lag spikes. Core set:
```
java -Xms<N>G -Xmx<N>G \
 -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 \
 -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:+DisableExplicitGC -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch \
 -XX:G1NewSizePercent=30 -XX:G1MaxNewSizePercent=40 -XX:G1HeapRegionSize=8M \
 -XX:G1ReservePercent=20 -XX:G1HeapWastePercent=5 -XX:G1MixedGCCountTarget=4 \
 -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=15 -XX:G1MixedGCLiveThresholdPercent=90 \
 -XX:G1RSetUpdatingPauseTimePercent=5 -XX:SurvivorRatio=32 \
 -XX:+PerfDisableSharedMem -XX:MaxTenuringThreshold=1 \
 -Dusing.aikars.flags=https://mcflags.emc.gs -Daikars.new.flags=true \
 -jar server.jar nogui
```
- Set `Xms == Xmx` (Aikar's guidance).
- **For >12 GB heaps**, switch to the large-heap variant: `G1NewSizePercent=40 G1MaxNewSizePercent=50 G1HeapRegionSize=16M G1ReservePercent=15 InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=20`.
- **Important 2026 caveat:** on **Java 25 / MC 26.1+**, don't blindly apply the classic Aikar set — newer JVMs prefer a modernized flag set (some hosts auto-swap). Consider ZGC/Generational-ZGC as an option only for very large heaps; G1+Aikar still wins for typical servers.
Sources: [version_manifest.json wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Version_manifest.json), [Paper Fill v3](https://docs.papermc.io/misc/downloads-service/), [Fabric meta](https://github.com/FabricMC/fabric-meta), [NeoForge server docs](https://docs.neoforged.net/user/docs/server/), [Bedrock Dedicated Server wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Bedrock_Dedicated_Server), [Aikar's flags (WinterNode)](https://winternode.com/help/games/minecraft-java/configuration/aikars-flags), [Space-node Aikar 2026](https://space-node.net/blog/aikar-flags-best-jvm-arguments-minecraft-2026)

---

## 5. Resource baseline (RAM/CPU per tier)

**Governing fact:** Minecraft's main simulation runs on **one thread**, so **single-core CPU clock speed is the primary TPS limiter** — RAM does not buy TPS, it buys headroom (more chunks/entities/mods before GC thrash). Prioritize high-clock CPUs (and pin cores) over core count for the sim thread; extra cores help chunk-gen (C2ME), GC, and co-located servers.

**RAM tiers — Vanilla / Paper (per current 2026 guidance ~200 MB/player + base):**
| Players | Vanilla/Paper RAM |
|---|---|
| 1–5 | 2–4 GB |
| ~10 | 4 GB |
| 10–30 | 4–8 GB |
| 30–60 | 8–12 GB |
| 50+/big | 12 GB+ |

**RAM tiers — Modded (scale ≈2× vanilla; RAM is driven by mod count, not just players):**
| Pack size | RAM |
|---|---|
| Light (≤~50 mods) | 6–8 GB |
| Medium | 8–10 GB |
| Heavy "kitchen-sink" | 10–12 GB+ (16 GB common for large packs / many players) |

**Rules of thumb to encode in the wizard:**
- ~2–6 MB RAM per player just for their loaded chunks (default view-distance 10 ≈ 441 chunks/player).
- Modpacks: budget by pack (each pack's page usually lists a recommended server RAM) + player headroom, then round up.
- Never allocate the whole box to heap — leave RAM for OS + off-heap/GC (and for Java, don't over-allocate; huge heaps increase GC pause).
- CPU: sell/schedule by dedicated high-clock vCores; view-distance + simulation-distance are the two knobs that most directly trade CPU for player experience — expose them prominently and cap them by tier.
Sources: [MineStrator RAM 2026](https://minestrator.com/en/blog/article/minecraft-server-ram-2026-vanilla-paper-modded-gb), [PrismNodes RAM 2026](https://prismnodes.com/blog/how-much-ram-does-a-minecraft-server-need), [DatHost benchmarks 2026](https://dathost.com/blog/minecraft-server-performance-benchmarks-2026)

---

## 6. "What we're missing" verdict — highest-value additions

1. **Dynamic, API-driven version + software picker (with the 26.x year-versioning + channels).** Pull versions live from Fill v3 (Paper), Mojang manifest, Fabric meta, NeoForge Maven — never a hardcoded list. Add NeoForge as a first-class option (it's the modding standard now, distinct from Forge) and expose a snapshot/experimental channel toggle. This is table-stakes and the most likely current gap.
2. **One-click modpack installer backed by Modrinth + CurseForge search** (`.mrpack` via mrpack-install, CurseForge `.zip` via API, plus FTB/ATLauncher server packs). Auto-selects the right loader + version + RAM. This is the single biggest conversion driver for the modded market.
3. **Cross-play out of the box: Geyser + Floodgate one-click**, so a Java server accepts Bedrock players. Highest-impact single toggle for public servers and a strong differentiator.
4. **Curated one-click plugin/mod catalog** (the §2 starter set: EssentialsX, LuckPerms, WorldEdit/Guard, Vault, PlaceholderAPI, CoreProtect, BlueMap, spark, ViaVersion, DiscordSRV) + a searchable Modrinth/Hangar browser — instead of manual jar uploads.
5. **Performance-config presets tied to plan tier** — auto-apply Aikar's flags (with the Java 25 / >12 GB variants), sane Paper/Spigot/Bukkit defaults (per-player-mob-spawns, entity-activation ranges, tuned view/simulation-distance), and a one-click "optimize" that installs Lithium/FerriteCore/C2ME on Fabric/NeoForge. Plus a raw config file editor + RCON console for power users.
